title: Published clients
what: The Rust crate bmo-agency-client and the TypeScript package the repository publishes, generated from the OpenAPI document: every body as a type and a typed call for every route.

title: Unit command
what: The bmo-agency command bmo dispatches to: its nouns, their words, the flags they take and their exit codes, as docs/api.md states them.

title: Event stream
what: The one server-sent stream GET /events publishes as things happen, with every kind agency emits, and the events the TypeScript side publishes by the names the boundary gives them.

title: Hook points
what: The decisions agency hands up to a consumer at a registered point, turn-submitting and session-summarising among them, each with a default that does nothing when nobody registered.

title: HTTP boundary API
what: Every route agency answers on its control port, grouped by resource: agents, sessions, turns, runs, executions, places, providers, models, tiers, fallback, accounts, companions, workers, assignments and jobs, with their status codes. docs/api.md states them and the control routes answer them.

title: Harness plugin tools
what: The MCP server bmo-agency mcp serves with its two tools assign_worker and run_job, each a thin call of one route through the agency client.

title: Shared tables
what: The tables a consumer reads or writes beside agency: room_windows with the receiver, and runs, agent_log, run_records and agent_executions that carry a run's ledger, log lines, records and executions.

title: Provided tools
what: The procedures and read_rulebook tools agency hands the tool host, each a folder with its tool.toml and executable, over the one tool-call protocol agency's tools answer on standard input and output.
